newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU aide says UN Zaire inaction is a global scandal.
newsitem.headline: EU aide says UN Zaire inaction is a global scandal.

text.p: European Commissioner Emma Bonino accused the United Nations Security Council on Saturday of scandalous indifference to the fate of thousands of refugees in Zaire.
"I really wonder how they can sleep at night," said Bonino, the European Union's commissioner for humanitarian aid. "How do they explain their actions to their wives, to their children?"

Bonino was speaking to Reuters after the Security Council in New York passed a resolution earlier on Saturday that put off any immediate prospect of a multinational force being deployed in eastern Zaire.
"The states who prevented a force being deployed are an international scandal...an international disgrace," she said.

The European Commission had wanted the council to adopt a resolution calling for the immediate creation of a multinational task force, but the United States -- mindful of its ill-fated involvement in a similar force in Somalia -- said it needed more time to study the options.
The council instead called on U.N. members to lay the groundwork for a multinational force but postponed a decision on deployment until November 20.
"November 20...which year?" said Bonino who leaves with a EU mission later on Saturday for Zaire where she hopes to visit refugee camps in the east of the country.
"The Security Council representatives should keep in mind that hundreds of thousands of refugees stranded cannot spend the weekend in Long Island, as they do," she said.

They fled to eastern Zaire after the massacre of up to a million Tutsis and moderate Hutus in Rwanda two years ago while thousands more escaped continuing violence between Hutus and Tutsis in neighbouring Burundi.

Thousands of them have now fled recent fighting between the Zairean army and Zairean ethnic Tutsis, backed by the Rwandan army. The conflict has spread death, fear and misery across a vast stretch of the biggest country in Central Africa.
Bonino said she was travelling to Zaire to get a first-hand account of the situation, but said she was at a loss how to explain her mission to the refugees.
"God knows what I will tell them," she said. "How can I tell them the Security Council doesn't see...doesn't listen...doesn't care."
She said Washington's reluctance to get involved in the conflict should not have delayed a Security Council decision on a force.

"If they don't want to be part, then fine -- but don't stop the others," she said. But she stressed that any action needed to be U.N.-driven in order to give the situation: "the international impetus it so desperately requires".
Bonino backs the idea of a force to patrol so-called "aid corridors" so that relief can be given to the refugees.
"We have the food for them," Bonino said. "But we have to be able to get it to them. Every day, every hour is costing lives."
